narrationScript: Now it's your turn to get hands-on and enhance our message board with persistent storage. In this first part of the lab, we'll focus on setting up Flask-SQLAlchemy and defining our database model. Your task is to open your `app.py` file from the previous chapter and make the following modifications. First, you'll need to import `SQLAlchemy` from `flask_sqlalchemy` and also `datetime` to handle timestamps for our messages. Next, configure your Flask application by adding the line `app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///site.db'`. This tells Flask-SQLAlchemy where to create and connect to your SQLite database file. After that, initialize your SQLAlchemy instance by calling `db = SQLAlchemy(app)`. Finally, define the `Message` database model exactly as shown in the lesson content. This involves creating a Python class that inherits from `db.Model` and defining the `id`, `text`, `author`, and `date_posted` columns with their respective data types and properties like `primary_key`, `nullable`, and `default`. Take your time to understand each part of the model definition, as this forms the blueprint for your database table.
